why: THREE STATES, AND ALL THREE EXIST BECAUSE THE GENERATED CORPUS PUT THE
STAGE-2 RAMP ON THE WRONG SIDE OF ITS OWN `sigma` CALL. The first sweep
scored 92 of 106 and the survivor list partitions almost exactly three ways:
line 241/242  the PRC_R_Speed sigma call      6 survivors
line 147      the freewheel low-speed test    2 survivors
line 194/308  the `SU_Stage <= N+1` guards    2 survivors
line 105/256  four true equivalences          4 survivors
SIX OF THE SURVIVORS ARE ONE FACT ABOUT `sigma`, not six defects in the
corpus. `sigma(x, x0, x1, y0, y1)` returns `y0` outright when `x < x0`, and
in every stage-2 case the generator produced, `LocalVar%Time` was below
`LocalVar%SU_LoadStageStartTime`. So the call returned `y0` regardless of
`x1` and `y1` -- which makes every mutation of the ramp-end expression
(`LSST + SU_LoadRampDuration(SU_Stage-1)`, its subscript, and the `1.0`
that is `y1`) invisible. `drop_factor` on `y0` was killed on 624 cases in
the same sweep, from the other side of the same call: what the corpus
reached was the y0 return and nothing past it.
State 2 puts `Time` INSIDE `[x0, x1]` so the cubic runs and every argument
of the call reaches the answer; state 3 puts it PAST `x1` so the `y1`
return is reached as well. Two states rather than one because those are two
different arms of `sigma`, and a single `Time` cannot be in both.
THE THRESHOLD ON THE FREEWHEEL TEST LOOKED UNREACHABLE AND IS NOT, and the
route is unit #41's, reused. `LocalVar%SU_RotSpeedF < 0.95 * SU_RotorSpeedThresh`
compares a value this unit COMPUTES against one it is given, so R6's
relational-pair rule -- which needs BOTH sides to be inputs -- cannot put it
at equality, and `'<' -> '<='` and `'0.95' -> '1.95'` both survived 7103
cases. But `LPFilter`'s initialisation arm returns its input BIT-EXACTLY at
`CornerFreq = 0`: the coefficients become a1 = 2, a0 = -2, b1 = b0 = 0 and
the expression collapses to `(1/2)*(2x)`, both operations exact. State 1
sets `SU_RotorSpeedCornerFreq = 0` with `iStatus = 0`, which turns the
computed side back into an input, and then sets `RotSpeed = 0.95` against
`SU_RotorSpeedThresh = 1.0` so that `0.95 * 1.0` is the same bits.
`iStatus = 0` DOES NOT COST THE `SU_Stage == 1` CONJUNCT, which is the part
worth checking rather than assuming: it forces `SU_Stage = -1` two
statements earlier, and the statement between them promotes -1 to 1 whenever
`Time > SU_StartTime`. So state 1 arrives at the freewheel test in stage 1
by the reference's own route.
R5's ARRAY-ELEMENTS-DISTINCT RULE IS OBSERVED -- all three SU_ ramps below
have a non-zero step. Unit #38's first baseline wrote a constant ramp and
made ten index mutants unkillable, because with every element equal `A[i-1]`
and `A[1-i]` return the same number.
`SU_LoadStages_N` IS 0 IN STATES 2 AND 3, WHICH LOOKS WRONG AND IS THE
POINT. The two `'1' -> '2'` survivors at lines 194 and 308 both widen
`SU_Stage <= SU_LoadStages_N + 1` to `+ 2`, so they change an answer only
where `SU_Stage == SU_LoadStages_N + 2`. With `SU_Stage` pinned to [-1, 4]
by harness/ranges.toml and `SU_LoadStages_N` to [0, 3], the smallest such
pair is (2, 0) -- and stage 2 is also the only stage on which the `sigma`
arm above runs. One state serves both.
`objInst_instLPF` IS NAMED because an unnamed varied parameter is
inert-filled to 0, and 0 is not an admissible filter slot: LPFilter would
subscript element -1 of six DIMENSION(1024) arrays. `CntrPar_PC_RefSpd` is
named for the same class of reason -- it is a DIVISOR, and 0 there makes
the stage-1 setpoint infinite.
WHAT THESE STATES DO NOT REACH, stated here rather than left to the score:
the four remaining survivors are declared equivalent in
harness/equivalences.Startup.json, and two of the four are properties of
LPFilter rather than of this unit.

states.name: freewheel_at_the_speed_threshold
states.why: iStatus = 0 with SU_RotorSpeedCornerFreq = 0 makes LPFilter the identity, so SU_RotSpeedF is RotSpeed to the bit; RotSpeed = 0.95 against SU_RotorSpeedThresh = 1.0 puts the freewheel test exactly on its threshold. SU_Stage arrives at 1 by the reference's own -1 -> 1 promotion, because Time = 100 is past SU_StartTime = 0. SU_LoadStageStartTime = 7 differs from Time, so the write that test guards is observable, and SU_FW_MinDuration = 50 makes the NEXT test answer differently depending on whether it happened: 100 >= 50 + 7 fires, 100 >= 50 + 100 does not.

states.name: load_stage_two_inside_the_ramp
states.why: SU_Stage = 2 with Time = 5 between SU_LoadStageStartTime = 0 and the ramp end 0 + SU_LoadRampDuration(1) = 10, so the PRC_R_Speed sigma call runs its CUBIC arm and every one of its arguments reaches the answer. The stage-advance test does not fire (5 < 0 + 10 + 20), so SU_Stage stays 2 and the arm is not left behind by the increment. SU_LoadStages_N = 0 makes SU_Stage == SU_LoadStages_N + 2, which is where the two `+1 -> +2` guard mutants change an answer; the torque chain's own guard therefore refuses to write, and PRC_R_Torque = 42 is what a mutant that writes has to disagree with.

states.name: load_stage_two_past_the_ramp_and_the_hold
states.why: The same stage-2 state with Time = 40, which is past the ramp end (10) so sigma returns y1 = 1.0 outright, and past the hold end (0 + 10 + 20 = 30) so the stage-advance test's TIME conjunct is satisfied and only the `SU_Stage <= SU_LoadStages_N + 1` conjunct refuses. That is what makes the `+1 -> +2` mutant at line 194 advance the stage when the reference does not -- and the difference then shows up in three compared outputs at once (SU_Stage, SU_LoadStageStartTime, PRC_R_Speed), because the advanced stage leaves the sigma arm entirely.
